subject.title: Session Routing Bugs: CLI routing to wrong session, WeChat ID inconsistency, and session deadlock from message flooding

question: Should this bundled report stay as a tracking umbrella, or should maintainers split it into separate TUI default-session, `sessions_send` channel, WeChat/plugin routing, background-event isolation, and activity-timestamp items before implementation?
rationale: The source gaps are real, but one PR cannot safely choose the TUI session contract, WeChat external-plugin boundary, `sessions_send` fix path, background-event isolation policy, and session activity taxonomy without maintainer product/ownership direction.

options.title: Split into focused owners
options.body: Keep this issue open as a temporary umbrella while maintainers split and route the timestamp, TUI, WeChat, `sessions_send`, and flood/deadlock work to focused canonical items.

options.title: Use this as canonical umbrella
options.body: Keep all subproblems on this issue and require any fix PR to explicitly cover or defer each reported behavior with proof.

options.title: Defer pending live WeChat repro
options.body: Pause code work until a maintainer or plugin owner reproduces the WeChat-specific routing and flooding failures on current main.

recommendation.title: Split into focused owners
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as a temporary umbrella while maintainers split and route the timestamp, TUI, WeChat, `sessions_send`, and flood/deadlock work to focused canonical items.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp already reviewed and landed the adjacent WeChat selector-boundary fix and is the clearest history-backed owner for deciding whether the remaining behavior belongs in core or the external WeChat plugin.
